messages.author: d4ec8fabba92d72e
messages.subject: NAs in produced latent variables
parts:
Dear Lavaan users,

I'am trying to fit a SEM model with multiple latent variables. The model below ran well and the multiple indices indicated a good model.
However, when i try to extract the latent variables from the model, I find a great amount of NAs in extracted latent variables (about 40% of produced LVs are missing)

Is there any problem in my code.

Thank you for the help

model_ALL<-'
Gsm=~X1+X2+X3+X4
Gc=~Y1+Y2+Y3+Y4+Y5
Gps=Z1+Z2+Z3
Gf=~W1+W2
Gv=~V1+V2+V3
Glr=~F1+F2+F3+F4+F5+F6+F7
Gs=~S1+S2
Gsm~A1+A2+A3+A4+A5
Gc~A1+A2+A3+A4+A5
Gps~A1+A2+A3+A4+A5
Gf~A1+A2+A3+A4+A5
Gv~A1+A2+A3+A4+A5
Glr~A1+A2+A3+A4+A5
Gs~A1+A2+A3+A4+A5
X1~~X2
Y5~~Y3+X4+X2+X1
Y4~~X4+X2+X1
Y1~~Y2
V1~~V2
F1~~F2+F3+F4
F3~~F4
'

fit_ALL=sem(model_ALL,data=dataset,estimator="MLR",missing="fiml")
summary(fit_ALL,fit.measures=T,standardized=T)
latent_ALL=as.data.frame(lavaan:::lavPredict(fit_ALL,type="lv"))


Youssef Oulhote

messages.author: 99a06696c483481a
messages.subject: RE: NAs in produced latent variables
parts:
Youssef—

     You are using FIML to deal with incomplete data.  FIML is not an imputation technique—it does not create values for the missing observations.  The “factor scores” that you request are weighted sums of the observed variables.  If the variables being summed include NAs, then the sum itself will be NA.

     If you don’t want this to happen, you could try a multiple imputation technique to deal with the incomplete observations.  Such an approach will assign a value to every data point, as long as the technique works.  However, any resolution of an imputation technique is just one possible outcome—run the process again (with random seed), and you will get somewhat different values.

--Ed Rigdon

I actually thought that the FIML creates new values for the missing observations using a multiple imputation technique.
I will maybe impute these missing values using the multiple imputation by chained equations. However, I'am wondering if there is a way to combine outputs from lavaan after using this technique that generates multiple datasets.

Thank you

Youssef
